case.why_ai_cites_it: It closes the theory that violating a terms-of-service clause is a federal crime, and it is the Supreme Court backing behind the scraping practices that produced most large training corpora.

reading.body:
Van Buren v. United States, a 2021 case narrowing the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act, holds that exceeding authorized access means reaching areas of a computer that are off limits entirely, not using information you were allowed to obtain for a purpose the owner disliked.

It is cited in defense in both Amazon.com Services lawsuits against Perplexity AI tracked here, which is a much narrower application than the 79-case pool behind the fair use precedents in this collection, since this one closes off only the federal criminal theory specifically rather than the underlying scraping practice itself. Its own stated limit says exactly that. A narrower CFAA leaves breach of contract as the live claim, meaning terms of service still bind even though violating them is no longer a federal crime.

The data does not report the current status of either Amazon lawsuit, only that both currently rely on this precedent for the same narrow point.
